title: Craticula GridSchema
description: The host-declared field allowlist and per-field configuration every compilation requires (SC-1..SC-5). This is a spec-level assumption authored for the conformance fixture suite (#1630) ahead of the actual GridSchema model/validator (#1631) — #1631 must conform to this shape, not the other way around, since this schema exists first. That precedence applies to what existed then; members added later were added here and in the model by the same story ('source' in #1638, per-field 'format' in #1653), so for those two the two are one change and neither leads. Every field a compilation touches (in filters, sort, group, aggregations) MUST appear in 'fields'; a colId absent from 'fields' is what the allowlist (SC-1) exists to reject.

mode.description: SC-1: Strict throws on an unlisted colId; Lenient silently strips it. Strict is the default per the TRD's own [DEFAULT] marker.

source.description: The physical collection every compiled query reads from: the SQL table or view named in FROM, the MongoDB collection, the Search index. Host-declared and never client-influenced — exactly like the per-field 'physical' mappings (SC-4) beside it, which is why it belongs here and not on the wire request: no AG Grid payload carries it and a compiler cannot invent it. Required — a query with no source cannot be emitted at all. Added in #1638: before it existed, every expected artifact in the fixture suite named a table ('FROM employees') that appeared in none of that fixture's inputs, recoverable only from the directory name.

stableKey.description: SEM-6: the field appended as a trailing sort tiebreaker whenever the request's own sort doesn't already end in a unique key. Required per grid — every GridSchema fixture must declare one, and it must itself be a key present in 'fields'.

staticFilter.description: SC-5: a host-authored IR filter fragment ANDed into every compiled query (the tenancy/soft-delete hook). Never client-influenced — this field only ever appears in schema.json, never in an agGridRequest.json. Absent means no static filter for this fixture.

fields.description: SC-2: the exhaustive allowlist, keyed by logical colId.

type.description: The declared type used by the AG Grid adapter to coerce this field's wire values into a typedValue (SEM-5) — matches the type tags in ir.schema.json's $defs/typedValue one-for-one.

aggregatable.description: Subset of AR-8's closed v1 aggregation functions this field may be aggregated with. Empty/absent means not aggregatable.

physical.description: SC-4: per-backend physical mapping. A field need only declare mappings for the backends the fixture actually targets.

text.description: SC-3: only meaningful when type is 'string'.

exportable.description: EXP-1: whether this field is included by default in a CSV/TSV export when the request's exportColumns is absent (§6.1: 'all schema fields flagged exportable are emitted in schema order'). true by default.

label.description: EXP-1: the export header text for this field when exportColumns doesn't supply its own header override ('headers from schema labels'). Falls back to the field's colId when absent.

format.description: EXP-5: per-field format overrides for the CSV/TSV writer. Absent means the invariant-culture default. Host-declared and never client-influenced — no AG Grid request carries a format, which is why EXP-5 puts the override in schema config. Like 'label', it reaches no compiler and appears in no expected artifact: page-export/026 is 013's inputs with these overrides added and pins a byte-identical postgres.artifact.json. Added in #1653.

sql.description: SC-4: plain column, qualified column (t.col), or a raw SQL expression escape hatch — always declared server-side, never client-influenced.

keywordSubField.description: SC-3: the .keyword-style exact-match/substring sub-field name, for term/wildcard/prefix/regexp ops on an analyzed field.

normalizedSubField.description: SC-3 (plural sub-field names): a keyword sub-field maintained via an ICU-folding normalizer at index time, used for case-insensitive ORDER BY / range comparisons (SEM-1) where ES/OpenSearch's query-time case_insensitive parameter is unavailable (range queries, in the pinned 7.10-era subset). Distinct from keywordSubField — only declare it for a field that needs case-insensitive ordering.

formatOptions.description: EXP-5's two per-field overrides, and only those two: the requirement names a date pattern and a decimal separator, so a third (thousands separator, boolean spelling, culture name) would be an invention every language port then has to reproduce.

datePattern.description: EXP-5's date pattern, replacing the writer's ISO 8601 default for this field only. Only meaningful when type is 'date' or 'datetime'. Written in the LDML/CLDR field letters every platform's formatter shares — yyyy, MM, dd, HH, mm, ss and literal separators — so 'dd/MM/yyyy' means the same to .NET, Java and a JavaScript port; a pattern outside that shared subset is not portable and must not appear in a fixture. A pattern no formatter can apply is rejected when the schema is parsed, not when the first date cell is written, which a streaming export cannot recover from. Note that an offset specifier (z/K) renders the host machine's offset when applied to a value that carries none, so it is meaningful only for a column an adapter yields with an offset.

decimalSeparator.description: EXP-5's decimal separator for this field, overriding the writer-wide default ('.', invariant culture). Only meaningful when type is 'decimal' or 'double' — an integral value has no fractional part to separate. Equal to the writer's active delimiter this is EXP-5's collision, and it is the same defect as the writer-wide one: the export is refused before its first byte by the writer, the only party that knows the delimiter. See schemas/writer-config.schema.json for the writer-wide default this overrides.

caseSensitivity.description: SEM-1: per-field opt-in to case-sensitive comparison; insensitive is the IR-level default.

searchMode.description: SEM-7: substring is contains' pinned default (wildcard/ngram); analyzed is the explicit per-field opt-in to tokenized relevance matching.
